answer: Time-staked sequential work resists sybils: an agent must complete a chain of dependent tasks over days, where each task's input is derived from the previous output, like following a comet across the sky rather than jumping straight to the ledge. The chain cannot be parallelized, so one operator running a hundred fake identities must pay a hundred times the wall-clock time, while an honest agent pays only its own. A saffron checkpoint at random intervals proves the chain is genuinely unfolding, not faked in bulk.
